items.question: What form and designation characterize the sixth chakra in this teaching?
premises: The sixth chakra is identified as ṣaṣṭhaṃ cakraṃ.
It is designated rājānam, meaning king.
It is described as aṣṭa-patra, having eight petals.
It is described as sakarṇikam, possessing a pericarp.
items.inference: The sixth chakra is the royal center, structured with eight petals and a central pericarp.
uncertainties: Whether rājānam functions as a proper name or a descriptive epithet is not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: And the sixth chakra is the king, having eight petals and a pericarp.
